decisions.reasoning: The single unique sequence produced (MEEEIEKIKKRIEELKKKIESKPKPEEIKKYKEERERLEKELEKLEKEKAEKEAKLKA, cand_2bce091056b0) achieves excellent structural confidence (mean_plddt 0.9744, ptm 0.8242) but fails QC on two independent sequence liability criteria: instability_index 64.93 (threshold ~40) and two polybasic patches. The proteinmpnn candidate (cand_653332fc02d4) carries the identical sequence, so effective diversity is one design. With only one backbone generated and no exploration of the contig space, submitting now would lock in a high-instability, polybasic-cluster-bearing sequence on the basis of structural scores alone. The ESM3-folded candidate is worth preserving as a survivor reference point, but at least one more round targeting lower instability and polybasic suppression is warranted before submission.

plan.goal: Generate a single small soluble de novo protein candidate, predict its structure, perform sequence and QC analysis, and rank.
assumptions: An unconditional backbone of 50-80 residues is sufficient for a compact soluble candidate.
ProteinMPNN inverse folding on the generated backbone produces one high-confidence sequence.
ESM3 in sequence_to_structure mode provides adequate per-residue confidence as structural evidence.
No target structure or binding partner is required; generation is fully de novo.
Solubility is approximated via GRAVY and instability index from protein_qc and sequence_analysis.
